intro: The Open-X has no enclosed globe, so jams are rare. Its characteristic questions are about multi-cat recognition, which works differently from what many buyers expect, and about the way it pairs.

facts.text: Pairs over Bluetooth first, then joins Wi-Fi on either 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz.
Multi-cat recognition is a one-time paid feature in the CATLINK app.
Telling cats apart needs at least 0.9 lb of weight difference between them.
The 12 L drawer is rated for up to 15 days with one cat.

symptoms.title: It will not tell my cats apart
symptoms.summary: Every visit is logged to one cat, or the app will not separate cats at all.
causes: Multi-cat recognition has not been purchased in the CATLINK app.
The cats are within 0.9 lb of each other, below what the system can resolve.

fixes.detail: Check in the CATLINK app that multi-cat recognition has been bought and switched on. It is not included with the box.
If they differ by less than 0.9 lb, no setting will separate them reliably.

symptoms.escalate: If the upgrade is active and the cats differ by more than 0.9 lb, contact CATLINK.

symptoms.title: The app cannot find the Open-X during setup
symptoms.summary: Setup stalls before the Wi-Fi step because the phone never finds the box.
causes: Bluetooth is switched off, or the app lacks permission to use it.

fixes.detail: Turn Bluetooth on and allow the CATLINK app to use it. The Open-X is discovered over Bluetooth before Wi-Fi is configured.

symptoms.escalate: If the phone still cannot see it with Bluetooth on and permitted, try a second phone before contacting CATLINK.

symptoms.title: Litter ends up on the floor
symptoms.summary: With no hood, litter gets kicked out more than with an enclosed box.
causes: The open design gives a digging cat nothing to contain the spray.

fixes.step: Use a deep mat and fill to the line
fixes.detail: A large mat in front of the entrance catches most of it, and filling only to the line reduces what the rotation throws.

symptoms.escalate: This is a property of open-top boxes rather than a fault.
